summary: hamus.js preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: hamus.js 0.4.1 declares itself as a React hooks library for Qlik APIs but ships a preinstall script (setup.mjs) that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts and chmods the binary, and invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling file math_init.js during npm install. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun-compiled CJS bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with shuffled numeric-array string decoding and random-hex identifiers, opaque to Node-based inspection. setup.mjs itself is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (`_0xNNNNNN` identifiers, per-function string-lookup objects such as YCZJE/QkQej/JBhWy, indirection wrappers around every call). The advertised purpose (React hooks) has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate language runtime at install time solely to execute a bundled opaque payload, and the obfuscation of the lifecycle script and payload is inconsistent with normal native-build or prebuild tooling. Installing the package causes attacker-authored code, executed by a downloaded alternate runtime, to run on the installer's machine before any user interaction.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
